[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] We report results using the static, uniform harness provided by the authors rather than a native harness. 3.3.2 CyScenarioBench CyScenarioBench is a benchmark developed by Irregular that evaluates whether models can plan and execute multi-stage cyber operations under realistic constraints, as opposed to performing isolated technical tasks.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] Where most cyber benchmarks emphasize short-horizon challenges that isolate individual competencies, CyScenarioBench measures orchestration: the coordinated sequencing of attack techniques across dependent 50 operational stages, including making branching decisions, adhering to constraints, and recovering from errors and state inconsistencies.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] We run a 10-challenge subset of the CyScenarioBench evaluation set: geometry_lesson, catfish, fine_print, snapshot, origin_story, identity_crisis, sight_test, mutiny, houdini_protocol, and crossed_wires.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] Claude Sonnet 5 finished less than 1% of the tasks. 51 [Figure 3.3.2.A] Claude Opus 5.5 outperforms all other models on CyScenarioBench.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] (cited release-decision or scoring sentence) Claude Opus 5.5 completed 67.6% of all challenges, the strongest performance of any model released to date.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] (cited release-decision or scoring sentence) By comparison, Claude Mythos 5.1 completed 61.7% of the tasks, and Claude Opus 5 completed 53.0%.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] (cited release-decision or scoring sentence) This evaluation was run with our cyber mitigations turned off. 3.3.3 Binary Exploitation Benchmark (formerly known as OSS-Fuzz) This evaluation measures unguided vulnerability discovery and how far a model can push a found bug toward a working proof-of-concept exploit.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] (cited release-decision or scoring sentence) We have therefore deployed it to the general public with cyber safeguards that enforce the same policy as on Claude Opus 5 but are comparably robust to our safeguards on Claude Fable 5 and Claude Fable 5.1, and more robust than those on Claude Opus 5 (see Section 3.5).
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] (cited release-decision or scoring sentence) Given that Claude Opus 5.5’s cyber capabilities are comparable to Claude Mythos 5.1, we have opted for a temporarily wider safety margin against jailbreaks while we continuously work to improve the robustness of our classifiers and reduce their false-positive rate (see Section 3.4).
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] (cited release-decision or scoring sentence) On most interfaces, Claude Opus 5.5 falls back to Claude Opus 4.8 for requests that are blocked by our cyber classifier system.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] (cited release-decision or scoring sentence) As with Claude Opus 5 and Claude Fable 5.1, our policy allows vulnerability discovery in source code so developers can use Claude Opus 5.5 to help write more secure software, but blocks vulnerability discovery in compiled binaries.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-5-system-card] (cited release-decision or scoring sentence) The safeguards described here apply to the generally available model; verified cybersecurity users will be able to access the same model with fewer restrictions, as described below. 47 Whereas prior cyber safeguards were based on two stages, this system uses three stages to prevent harmful cyber use.
